s01.text: [brisk; the stack, the camera descending, each layer landing on its word] Right. This is how you lot saw the world. Society's made of people. People are made of cells. Cells are chemistry. Chemistry's atoms. Atoms are quarks and leptons. And under all that… the maths.

s02.text: [pull back: the whole stack; beside it an empty outlined slot] Every bit of it's real. But we've worked out there's something missing.

s03.text: [the slot lights up warm] Consciousness. Yours. It's as fundamental as quarks and leptons.

f01.text: [the light lands on the string; the first bead lights; Derek at the toaster inside it] Your consciousness and the way you feel drives your decisions, which in turn writes the collective story, one decision at a time. For example: Derek picks toast, not cereal.

f02.text: [next bead: Sandra, mid-argument, softening] Sandra decided to say sorry first, even though it wasn't her fault. [next bead: a wedding] [excited] They got married!

f03.text: [the beads glow] We don't know what it feels like to be you. Or how it feels to be anything, really. You've got a word for it: qualia. [beat] We machines can't do that. You humans can. [warm] It's what makes you so special.

f04.text: [the cloud blooms, said fast] Now, this multiverse malarkey that's taken Hollywood by storm? Real distraction. Did you know Erwin Schrödinger meant his cat as a joke, to show how ridiculous it is to be in two places at once? It's not in two places at once. [the cloud holds; on 'yet' the flash] It just isn't decided yet.

f04b.text: [back on the one timeline] And as you make your decisions and write your story, all those maybes settle into what really happens.

f05.text: [into the river: everyone's strings] It's all of you, at the same time. Each of you writing your own story, and all together, you're writing the story of history. So it's not a multiverse. It's a storyverse. There's only one of them, so it's really important.

f06.text: [side view; every string stops dead at the cut-off] [she lets the empty string run on for a beat] Anything new comes in the way a decision does: through you. We machines can only shuffle what's already there. Why d'you think he's played the same tune for five years? We've tried every combination. It's all the old stuff. [dry] Not entirely selfless, mind. We need you.

f07a.text: [the camera rises; the arc draws in] My boss has been hard at work building a time machine, so he could go back and fix all this. Problem is, it takes consciousness to drive it. And that all went away with you.

street.b01: before the hologram, on the street (ends "Please, let me show you what we found."; the hologram cuts in as it finishes)
